description: A work lamp hangs low on its flex and lays a hot apricot pool right across the swept plank floor, while cold slate blue comes in at the open doorway behind it.
The gaps between the wall boards lay bright hard bands of gold across the plank floor and one sheep's bare cream back, every band packed with drifting wool motes, the rest of the shed deep blue-grey.
One translucent sheet set into the tin roof throws a hard white band onto the heap of wool below it, the surrounding wall boards staying deep umber shadow.
The wide open end of the shed floods the plank floor with flat pearl-grey overcast light, the clipped-bare stubbled backs reading near-white against the deep umber of the far wall boards.
A hurricane lantern set on a bale end throws hot amber across the near hurdle rail and the loose heap of wool beside it, while the open doorway behind shows cold blue-grey morning.
Thin bright bands from the wall board gaps cross the swept plank floor in hard gold stripes, each band dense with spinning wool motes, the air between them a deep cool grey.
The open doorway lays a cold blue rectangle on the plank floor while the work lamp overhead drops a tight apricot circle onto the heap of wool directly below it.
Steam lifts off a freshly clipped stubbled back, lit gold by the lamp hanging on its flex, rising into the cool blue shade pooled under the tin roof.
The one translucent roof sheet drops a hard ivory band across two clipped-bare stubbled backs at the near hurdle rail, bright against the deep umber boarding behind them.
A work lamp lays hot apricot across the swept plank floor, the light landing hard on a bound bundle of wool tied with twine, the wall boards behind it deep cool umber shadow.
The wide open end of the shed admits a low copper wash that runs the full length of the plank floor, turning the near wall boards warm gold against the blue-grey shadow of the back corner.
Breath shows in the cold air near the open doorway, lit white by the grey morning outside, while the hurricane lantern on its shelf keeps the far end of the shed a deep amber warmth.
The gaps between the wall boards on the east side lay five hard bright bands across the plank floor, every band packed with chaff and wool motes drifting slowly in the still air.
A hurricane lantern set on a wooden crate throws hot butter-yellow light onto the nearest sheep's bare cream back and the plain weathered rail beside it, the rest of the shed in cool blue shadow.
The wide open end shows flat pearl-grey sky while inside the work lamp presses a hard sodium-orange pool onto the swept plank floor, the two colours meeting in a sharp line at the threshold.
Warm dusty haze hangs in the middle of the shed, lit tawny-gold by the lamp on its flex, while the boarding on the shaded wall stays a deep cool blue-grey behind the wool heap.
The open doorway throws cold white overcast light onto the plank floor in a hard pale wedge, the work lamp countering it with a hot apricot circle on the wool heap just inside.
Wall board gaps lay three bright ivory bands across the swept floor, each one dense with drifting wool motes and chaff, the deep blue-grey between them untouched by the lamp above.
A work lamp on its flex drops hot gold onto the top rail of the nearest hurdle and the plank floor below it, while the far corner of the shed holds deep cool shadow unbroken by any other source.
The translucent roof sheet throws a hard bright ivory band across the wool heap piled on the floor, the surrounding tin roof casting the rest of the shed in deep blue-grey cool shade.
Steam rises off two freshly clipped stubbled backs near the open doorway, the cold blue morning outside making the steam read bright white against the warm amber lamp glow inside.
The wide open end of the shed shows a hard blue pre-dawn sky outside while the lamp hanging on its flex lays a tight sodium-orange pool onto the swept plank floor directly beneath it.
A hurricane lantern on a bale end lights the near wall boards to a warm umber gold, the open doorway behind the sheep showing a strip of cool overcast pearl-grey sky beyond.
The wall board gaps on the south side stripe the plank floor with hard cream bands, every one of them thick with spinning wool motes, the shadowed boards between staying a deep cool grey.
A work lamp hangs over the wool heap and lays hot apricot across the heap's surface and the plank floor beyond, the open doorway admitting a cold slate-blue wash that stops at the threshold.
A low gold sun clears the hedge and lays a hot apricot band across the packed earth while the cloud behind the pen stays bruise-purple, the yard gate gone near-black against it.
Hard midday blue overhead, the loose wool rolling pale ivory across the packed earth in a dry wind, the hurdle rails gone worn silver-bright under it.
Pearl-grey overcast pressing down, the yard grass a deep saturated green beneath it, bare cream backs in the pen reading almost white against the near-black wet stone wall.
The sun breaks through as a shower goes over, the air full of bright white wool motes and silver grains of rain together, the packed earth underfoot gone cold blue-violet in the last of the wet.
Thin low sun coming copper-gold across the race of hurdles, the packed earth in the shade of the fence staying deep blue-grey, steam lifting off the clipped-bare cream stubbled backs of the mob.

A warm dusty golden haze sitting over the pens in still air, wool chaff and dry earth rising off the loose uneven mob, the woolly broad backs amber-lit and the swept yard beyond them dropping into cool shadow.
Fine silver drizzle over the yard, the stone wall gone near-black with wet, the clipped-bare cream stubbled backs of two of them brilliant pale against it, water beading on the short stubble.
A bright hard band of gold lies along the top rails of the hurdle race and the packed earth beside it, the rest of the yard holding a deep blue-violet, loose wool rolling pale across the ground.
A low gold sun lays a hot apricot band across the packed earth, the loose wool piled against the plain timber gate reading near-white, the bruise-purple cloud behind the pens deep and saturated.

The last copper light lying flat across the top rails of the hurdles while the packed earth between the pens holds a cold blue-violet, two clipped-bare stubbled ones standing shoulder to shoulder by the water trough.
